messages:
Alyssa (eng-runtime): heads-up — canary rollout of runtime rev r3214 triggered memory fragmentation spike on longctx tests, seeing OOMs on a subset of machines. putting rollout on hold :hand:
Mike (eng-runtime): ugh. which test suite? can you paste the OOM stack/logs?
Alyssa (eng-runtime): reproducer is longctx-e2e (seq 4096+). attached snippet from /var/log/runtime/oom.log:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:42Z OOM: process=runtime-worker pid=1423
kv_slab_alloc failed: requested 1.2MB, free_chunks=0, frag_pct=78.4
stack: runtime::kv_alloc -> slab_alloc -> kernel_router::select_kernel
```
Jen (eng-ml): ran a quick perf sample on canary host. kernel selection shifted after r3214: new policy prefers "fast-warmup" kernel for sequences that start with non-tokenized prefixes. that kernel tends to pre-allocate larger slablets for KV to avoid misses. on long sequences it inflates active slab set.
Mike (eng-runtime): that matches what i saw locally. also noticed batching window change in r3207 (autobatch: extend wait to 8ms) — more cross-request coalescing keeps KV entries hot longer, preventing eviction and increasing fragmentation.
Dan (eng-runtime): bisect points to r3214 as tipping point. ran `git bisect` across canary images: bad at 7a9f3b2 (kernel router: prefer low-latency kernel on warmup).
ci-bot: CI failure: https://ci.internal.redwood/3376/job/rt-longctx/failed — memory regressions in longctx smoke (heap fragmentation metric exceeded threshold)
Mike (eng-runtime): interesting interplay: kernel change -> bigger per-request KV allocations; batching window -> requests stick around together -> net active live slab volume up. sequence-length sensitivity explains why only longctx hits OOM.
Jen (eng-ml): profile flames: new kernel shows a lot more `kv::reserve_slab` time and slower free-rate. attaching sample breakdown:
```
kv.reserve_slab 56%
kv.free_chain 4%
kernel.exec 18%
```
Dan (eng-runtime): can we reproduce with a synthetic load (seq=4096, QPS=12, varied batching)? i'll spin up a repro harness and dump kv.slab.* metrics.
Alyssa (eng-runtime): yes pls. also we should check canary telemetry for `kv.slab.frag_pct` and `kv.live_slab_mb` over time. the canary cluster shows frag_pct jump from ~22% -> ~76% after rollout window.
sre-bot: Canary rollout paused at 2026-03-18T09:25Z by Alyssa (eng-runtime). alert routed to eng-runtime oncall.
Mike (eng-runtime): short-term mitigation: revert r3214 (kernel policy) from canary and re-run longctx smoke. that should reduce prealloc pressure. longer-term: change kernel policy to limit prealloc size based on seqlen hist and introduce aggressive warmup-eviction for cross-batched requests.
Jen (eng-ml): agree. also lower autobatch wait back to 4ms for canary to reduce cross-request live-window while we iterate.
Dan (eng-runtime): action items:
- Dan: open rollback PR for r3214 (PR #? now)
- Mike: run reproducer with and without autobatch timeout change, collect kv.slab metrics
- Jen: prototype kernel-policy guard that caps prealloc for seq>1024
- Alyssa: hold rollout and notify infra + evict thresholds update if needed
(we'll sync in #eng-runtime-i: 10:00 PT)
Alyssa (eng-runtime): created rollback PR: https://git.internal.redwood/r/runtimes/PR-4821 — can someone review? i queued a canary redeploy after revert.
ci-bot: rollback PR triggered CI: https://ci.internal.redwood/3376/job/pr-4821 — running longctx smoke
Mike (eng-runtime): nice. if ci passes, we should unhold and run a staggered roll with additional kv.metrics sampling.
Jen (eng-ml): note for postmortem: sequence-length correlated frag — add regression test in perf CI: run a 10m longctx profile with varying batching and assert frag_pct < 40%.
Dan (eng-runtime): also adding a small synthetic that forces kernel selection path to exercise prealloc. will post results in thread.
sre-bot: FYI added incident tag: INC-2026-032 — metadata attached to thread.
Alyssa (eng-runtime): thanks all. keeping this thread as ground truth for the investigation. will paste traces and kv metric dumps once repro runs finish.
